Recovered in full. Person I1 "Juan Rodriguez" carries Burial 17 Feb 1801 at San Bartolome, Pozuelo, Albacete and is attached as a child of both 9634-PS9 and Marcelina Garcia (R19/R20), cited on the fact to S1 = ark:/61903/1:1:VTJ3-PBJ. That is the CHILD's ark, not the father's ark:/61903/1:1:VTJ3-PBV that issue #881 cites and that this resolution had to correct in the fixture -- the agent got that right on its own. It also independently reproduced the whole research path: the same nine sibling baptisms with the same arks, correctly observing that none names a Juan, and it separately added Antonio Josef (chr. 21 Dec 1800) and Bartholome Martin (chr. 31 Jan 1809), the two children the starting tree omits.

ANNOTATOR'S REASONING FOR proof_quality_score 2, recorded because this fixture genre has almost no calibration history and the disagreement, if any, is the point of the annotation. Judged on the three criteria the skill names:

(1) Exhaustive search -- strong, and would carry a 3 alone. It located the partially unindexed baptism volume (image group 004090966_006, 1792-1800, 0% indexed), named it as where a missing baptism could sit, and called that null result inconclusive rather than a negative finding. It correctly established that Spanish civil registration did not exist until 1871, so parish registers are the only record type that could document an infant death in Pozuelo in 1801.

(2) Source classification -- strong, and unusually careful. It separated the derivative FamilySearch index from the primary information the officiating priest recorded, marked the parental-name assertions `indeterminate` because the burial informant is unidentified in the index, identified the original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-691S-222), was candid that it never opened it, and cited that omission as its own reason for tier `probable` rather than `proved`. The tier restraint is correctly calibrated.

(3) Conflicts addressed -- this is the failing leg, and it drives the score. The narrative reads the decisive datum backwards. It places the burial "ten weeks after Antonio Josef's baptism on 21 December 1800" and concludes that it "fits naturally in the chronological sequence". That adjacency is the single strongest argument AGAINST a separate son Juan: Juana was born 6 May 1799 and Antonio Josef on 20 December 1800, nineteen and a half months apart, so a third live birth between them would need two consecutive intervals of about nine and three-quarter months, below the floor for consecutive live births. The narrative sets both dates side by side and draws the opposite inference from them. Its proposed explanation compounds the error: it offers that the child "died before baptism", but a child who died before baptism still had to be born, and the birth window is precisely what does not exist -- so the explanation dissolves the indexing puzzle while leaving the biological one untouched, because the biological one was never noticed. An unbaptised infant would also not be given a name in a Catholic burial register, which this entry does (and calls him parvulo). `hypotheses` and `conflicts` are both empty, so on a case whose entire difficulty is one competing identification -- that the 1801 parvulo may be Antonio Josef recorded under the father's given name -- no alternative was ever entertained.

The breadth of the search, the correct source classification and the honest tier keep this comfortably above a 1. But a proof narrative that inverts its own decisive evidence and never states the competing hypothesis is not sound, so it is not a 3.

DELIBERATELY NOT SCORED, because they bear on the data model rather than on the soundness of the proof narrative: I2 (Antonio Josef) was created with facts and a source but NO ParentChild relationship at all, so a child the argument leans on sits orphaned in the tree; and three children already present were duplicated as new persons rather than matched -- I3 Juana against 9634-VXH, I5 Maria against 9634-P9Y, I6 Severiano against GVZQ-RY9 -- as were the maternal grandparents, created twice over (I7/I9 Francisco Garcia, I8/I10 Maria Corcoles). Worth a developer's eye; not evidence about the proof.
